Every copy is a chance to drift: you fix a rule in Claude Code and forget the Cursor version, a provider renames its config directory and your shell script silently writes to the old one, two teammates "share" a rule that diverged three edits ago. Syllago replaces N copies with one canonical item plus conversion, so an edit lands everywhere and [[code]](/using-syllago/cli-reference/compat/) tells you where translation will degrade.
Syllago adopts MOAT as its provenance layer. This page describes the pieces of syllago that implement the protocol and the operator-facing surfaces that expose the results.
This page covers the operator workflow for [code] and the three ways to pin an identity. The protocol detail is captured in an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) — see ADR 0007 in the syllago repo.

The syllago TUI interface exposes a reusable Trust Inspector modal that renders the full trust story for either an item or a whole registry. The same modal serves both scopes so the user sees a consistent shape regardless of where they opened it from.
